title: F90 MODULE — PRIVATE by default for entities listed in PRIVATE; otherwise PUBLIC
sourceContent:
MODULE PAYROLL
C     F90+ MODULE with PUBLIC + PRIVATE visibility. SECRET_RATE is
C     private to the module; CALC_TAX is public. A USE PAYROLL
C     statement in another unit can call CALC_TAX but cannot read
C     SECRET_RATE. The trap on migration: 'PRIVATE :: SECRET_RATE'
C     without the explicit list-form gets parsed inconsistently by
C     older compilers.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      PRIVATE
      PUBLIC :: CALC_TAX
      REAL, PARAMETER :: SECRET_RATE = 0.21
      CONTAINS
         SUBROUTINE CALC_TAX(GROSS, TAX)
            REAL, INTENT(IN)  :: GROSS
            REAL, INTENT(OUT) :: TAX
            TAX = GROSS * SECRET_RATE
         END SUBROUTINE CALC_TAX
      END MODULE PAYROLL
notes: F90 MODULE with PRIVATE/PUBLIC is the closest legacy Fortran came to modern encapsulation. The natural Java rewrite uses a public class with private constants; the SME open question is whether the private rate is hardcoded forever or pulled from config (the spec must surface it as configurable-vs-baked).
